title: Taxonomic Classification
standard_text: Living things are classified into domains and kingdoms and named with binomial nomenclature; taxonomic ranks from kingdom to species; dichotomous keys. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 8, Quarter 1: Life Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 1: Life Science): taxonomy and scientific names, domains and kingdoms, bacteria, viruses and protists, fungi and plants and animals and biodiversity. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Living things are grouped by shared features and evolutionary history.
key_sub: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.
body_html:
How to think about it

Biologists sort the huge variety of life into groups that share features and ancestry. The ranks go from broad to narrow: domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species. Every species has a two-part scientific name, the genus and the species, written in italics (Acer saccharum, the sugar narra).

The three domains are Bacteria, Archaea (both prokaryotes, with no nucleus) and Eukarya (cells with a nucleus). Eukarya includes protists, fungi, plants and animals. Viruses are not placed in any kingdom: they are not cells and can only reproduce inside a host cell.

Example

Which two ranks make up a scientific name?

Binomial nomenclature uses the genus and the species.

Answer: genus and species

Example

A cell has no nucleus and lives in a hot spring. Which domains are possible?

No nucleus means prokaryote.

Answer: Bacteria or Archaea

Common mistakes

  • Writing the genus with a small letter or not using italics.
  • Calling viruses bacteria: viruses are not cells.
  • Thinking that fungi are plants: fungi do not photosynthesize and have chitin cell walls.

faq.a: Fungi have cell walls made of chitin, cannot photosynthesize and absorb food from their surroundings.

items.q: Which description fits kingdom Animalia?
c: multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food
heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin
multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food
items.e: Animalia: multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food.

items.q: What is a herbarium?
c: a garden of living plants grown and labeled for study
a store of pressed, dried and labeled plant specimens on sheets
a book that helps identify the species in an area
items.e: herbarium: a store of pressed, dried and labeled plant specimens on sheets.

items.q: What is a flora?
c: an account of the plant species found in an area
a book that helps identify the species in an area
a tool that identifies organisms using pairs of contrasting characters
items.e: flora: an account of the plant species found in an area.

items.q: Which is a living thing that cannot reproduce?
items.e: A mule is sterile.

items.q: Which description fits kingdom Plantae?
c: prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan
multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food
multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food
items.e: Plantae: multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food.

items.q: Which kingdom has members that are unicellular eukaryotes?
items.e: Protista: unicellular eukaryotes.

items.q: Which taxonomic aid is a tool that identifies organisms using pairs of contrasting characters?
items.e: key: a tool that identifies organisms using pairs of contrasting characters.

items.q: Who proposed the five-kingdom classification?
items.e: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia (1969).

items.q: What are viroids?
c: free RNA without a protein coat that cause disease
items.e: Found by T. O. Diener; cause potato spindle tuber disease.

items.q: What is a monograph?
c: a place where wild animals are kept in protected surroundings like their natural habitat
a tool that identifies organisms using pairs of contrasting characters
an account of the plant species found in an area
items.e: monograph: information about any one taxon.

items.q: Which description fits kingdom Fungi?
c: heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin
multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food
prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan
multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food
items.e: Fungi: heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin.

items.q: What is a zoological park?
c: a book that helps identify the species in an area
a tool that identifies organisms using pairs of contrasting characters
a place where wild animals are kept in protected surroundings like their natural habitat
a collection of preserved plant and animal specimens
items.e: zoological park: a place where wild animals are kept in protected surroundings like their natural habitat.

items.q: In Mangifera indica, what does 'indica' stand for?
items.e: Mangifera is the genus.

a store of pressed, dried and labeled plant specimens on sheets

items.e: They can release toxins that kill fish.

items.q: Which group of plants is described as pteridophytes?
c: the first land plants with vascular tissue (xylem and phloem)
plants with naked seeds, not enclosed in an ovary
flowering plants with seeds enclosed in fruits
the amphibians of the plant kingdom
items.e: The first land plants with vascular tissue (xylem and phloem): pteridophytes.

items.q: Which group of plants is described as bryophytes?
c: plants with naked seeds, not enclosed in an ovary
the first land plants with vascular tissue (xylem and phloem)
flowering plants with seeds enclosed in fruits
the amphibians of the plant kingdom
items.e: The amphibians of the plant kingdom: bryophytes.

items.q: Which fungi belong to Deuteromycetes?
items.e: Deuteromycetes: Alternaria and Trichoderma.

items.q: Which is the dominant phase in pteridophytes?
items.e: The gametophyte is a small prothallus.

items.q: Which fungi belong to Phycomycetes?
items.e: Phycomycetes: Rhizopus and Albugo.

items.q: What is the tallest tree species?
items.e: Some are over 100 m tall.

items.q: What is the protonema?
c: the first, alga-like stage of a moss gametophyte
items.e: It grows from a spore.

items.q: What is double fertilization?
c: one male gamete fuses with the egg and another with the polar nuclei
items.e: It is unique to angiosperms.

items.q: To which class of fungi do Alternaria and Trichoderma belong?
items.e: Deuteromycetes: Alternaria and Trichoderma.

items.q: To which class of fungi do mushrooms, bracket fungi and smuts belong?
items.e: Basidiomycetes: mushrooms, bracket fungi and smuts.

items.q: Which group of plants is described as gymnosperms?
c: the amphibians of the plant kingdom
the first land plants with vascular tissue (xylem and phloem)
flowering plants with seeds enclosed in fruits
plants with naked seeds, not enclosed in an ovary
items.e: Plants with naked seeds, not enclosed in an ovary: gymnosperms.

items.q: Which plants are called flowering plants with seeds enclosed in fruits?
items.e: Flowering plants with seeds enclosed in fruits: angiosperms.

items.q: What is a haplontic life cycle?
c: the sporophyte is only the one-celled zygote; the gametophyte is dominant
items.e: Seen in Volvox, Spirogyra and some Chlamydomonas.

items.q: Which fungi belong to Ascomycetes?
items.e: Ascomycetes: Penicillium, Aspergillus and yeast.

items.q: Which group of plants is described as angiosperms?
c: the first land plants with vascular tissue (xylem and phloem)
plants with naked seeds, not enclosed in an ovary
flowering plants with seeds enclosed in fruits
the amphibians of the plant kingdom
items.e: Flowering plants with seeds enclosed in fruits: angiosperms.

items.q: Which fungi belong to Basidiomycetes?
items.e: Basidiomycetes: mushrooms, bracket fungi and smuts.

items.q: Which alga is a rich protein food supplement, even for space travelers?
items.e: It is unicellular and fast-growing.

items.q: What is the ploidy of the endosperm in angiosperms?
items.e: It forms from the fusion of a male gamete with two polar nuclei.

items.q: In which group do vascular tissues first appear?
items.e: They have true roots, stems and leaves.

items.q: To which class of fungi do Rhizopus and Albugo belong?
items.e: Phycomycetes: Rhizopus and Albugo.

items.q: Which is the largest phylum of the animal kingdom?
items.e: About two-thirds of all named species are arthropods.

items.q: Which feature is typical of phylum Mollusca?
c: a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus
a soft body covered by a calcareous shell and a mantle
jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton
items.e: Mollusca: a soft body covered by a calcareous shell and a mantle.

items.q: Which phylum shows a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus?
items.e: Hemichordata: a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus.

items.q: Which feature is typical of phylum Arthropoda?
c: the tissue level of organization and cnidoblasts (stinging cells)
jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton
a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus
items.e: Arthropoda: jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton.
